If you only remember one thing today, remember this. Meta agreed to pay up to seventeen billion dollars over harms to children. It's the largest child safety settlement in tech history. And it's the moment regulators stopped losing.

Item one. Meta's settlement is the story of the week.

Prosecutors from forty seven states, Washington D C, and U S territories reached a settlement with Meta. The claim was that Meta deliberately designed addictive products it knew were harming children. The floor is twelve billion dollars. The ceiling is seventeen point one billion. Meta also has to make design changes for underage users. So the money is not the whole penalty.

Your Tech Policy Press newsletter led with this too. Their headline said the settlement will reverberate across the world for years. That's the framing to steal. This isn't a fine. It's a template.

And it lands inside a wider losing streak. Meta lost two court cases this year over Instagram's effect on young users. Google's YouTube, TikTok and Snapchat have all settled similar suits. TikTok separately settled with the Justice Department for four hundred million dollars over illegally collecting kids' data.

Why it matters. For years the pattern was that tech pays a rounding error and moves on. A seventeen billion dollar figure, plus mandated product changes, breaks that pattern. Every comms team in the industry is rewriting its risk language this week.

Item two. The copyright bill comes due.

A federal judge approved Anthropic's one point five billion dollar settlement with authors over pirated books. That's the largest copyright recovery in U S history. Separately, litigation over viral A I generated characters is becoming a real test of human authorship, trademark, and who commercially owns something an A I made.

Why it matters. Training data is no longer a free input. It's a line item. And that changes who can afford to build a frontier model.

Item three. Chips. Washington moves on the rental loophole.

A U S agency is now systematically reviewing how Chinese A I firms access Nvidia chips they aren't allowed to buy. The method is renting compute in data centers abroad. Several Chinese firms reportedly reached top tier chips through facilities in Southeast Asia. A White House official accused Moonshot A I of exactly this, using a facility in Thailand. Proposed legislation, the Remote Access Security Act, would extend export controls to remote cloud access. It passed the House in January. It's still sitting in the Senate.

Meanwhile, more than seventy companies, led by Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, Dell and I B M, signed an open letter. They urged the administration not to broadly restrict open weight A I models. Their argument is that open models keep competition alive for smaller builders.

Why it matters. Export controls were written for boxes crossing borders. And the thing being exported now is a login.

Item four. From your Reads. China's A I week.

Recode China A I's weekly digest covered three things. Z dot A I claiming the mystery frontier model that had been circulating anonymously. DeepSeek reaching a seventy four billion dollar valuation. And Beijing hosting a robot olympics. Z dot A I's newest flash model, released August twenty sixth, currently sits at the frontier of recent releases.

Why it matters. The valuation and the frontier claim together say the export controls have slowed China's chips, not its models.

Item five. Model news and price moves.

OpenAI unveiled G P T five point five Omni, pushing further into real time multimodal interaction. It also cut the price of its Luna model by roughly eighty percent, to twenty cents in and one dollar twenty per million out. That's now the free default in Chat G P T. Anthropic moved Claude Sonnet five from two dollars to three dollars per million, effective today. And Google's Gemini app crossed one billion monthly active users earlier this month.

Why it matters. Prices are falling at the bottom and rising at the top. The market is splitting into cheap and everywhere, versus expensive and capable.

Item six. Google consolidates A I leadership.

Google is ending the two continent Brain and DeepMind split. Demis Hassabis steps back to Chairman. Koray Kavukcuoglu takes operations. And the coding team relocates from London to Mountain View.

Why it matters. DeepMind's London independence was a decade long promise. That's the top of the news. Your full briefing is in the recording.
